chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Asbat, who raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said:

One who recites a hundred verses from the Quran, from whichever part of the Quran he wishes, then says 'Ya Allah' seven times, even if he supplicates against a stone, it would be dislodged, if God wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward and method for reciting a hundred verses of the Quran followed by a specific invocation?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam Ali (AS) underscores the potency of combining Quranic recitation with the divine name 'Allah' to achieve *istijabah* (acceptance of supplication). The metaphor of dislodging a stone illustrates that this specific dhikr possesses the spiritual force to move physical obstacles, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of invoking God's greatest name with focused devotion.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali b. Majluwayh from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Ali b. Asbat who raised it to Ameer al-Mumineen (a.s.) who said: “
One who says Yaa Allaah seven times after reciting a hundred verses of the Holy Quran from anywhere, even if he prays against Sakhr (a stone) it would be dislodged from its place.”
